newsitem.title: UK: Russia undervalued on performance, fundamentals - ING.
newsitem.headline: Russia undervalued on performance, fundamentals - ING.

text.p: Russian equities are undervalued relative to the country's debt market and on fundamental value, ING Barings chief east Europe economist Philip Poole said in a note to investors.

Using the trading relationship between dollar Vneshekonombank loans and the Moscow Times 50 share index, Poole believes that the Russian equity market should be trading 20 percent above its current level.

"The regression is not a perfect model of the relationship between the two asset classes. Nonetheless, it supports our view that the Russian equity market is currently cheap relative to debt," he said.
On Monday, dollar Vneshekonombank was quoted at 79 cents, while the Moscow Times index in roubles was trading at around 328 points.
"On a fundamental view, in terms of absolute valuations, the equity market also looks like good value - but that has been the case for some time," Poole said.

However, he believes that some switching from the debt market in to equities, combined with new flows from foreign investors during the next three to six months will push equities higher, although gains are likely to be limited to counters which are listed overseas, or the blue chip shares quoted in Moscow.

"We still believe that this is not yet a stock-picker's market. While searching for value in the second-tier stocks will be the root to substantial longer term gains, in the short term, liquidity and a degree of name recognition will be the most important factors that both new investors and short-term switch players will prize," Poole said.
